name: Question 8
problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)-y{x}^{2},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+2xy⟩
$$

through the boundary of the square with vertices $(0,-1),(1,-1),(1,0),$ and $(0,0).$
worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062447/assets/3497b3bbc834879026235f97468f5feb26e91a2b73a4de3da87597bf422ecd33.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)-y{x}^{2}$ and $Q(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)+2xy.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=-2xy,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the rectangular region $D$ as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le y\le 0}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-2xy+2x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2x-2xy)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({x}^{2}-{x}^{2}y)\,{|}_{0}^{1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[(1-y)-0]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(1-y)\,dy \\  & =[y-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]_{-1}^{0} \\  & =0-((-1)-\frac{(-1)^{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
